page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m2.large is a general-purpose virtual machine hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon architecture operating at a 2.7 GHz clock speed, accompanied by 4.0 GB of system memory. This distribution establishes a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, aligning it with resource-dense, compute-oriented footprints in entry-level virtual tiers.

Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth capacity of 2 Gbps. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote block storage attachments for operating system installation and runtime storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs allocated, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Because processing cores are dedicated rather than shared or burstable, execution performance remains stable under consistent load. Cost efficiency is driven by the lean resource specification, minimizing infrastructure overhead for workloads that do not require expansive physical memory or specialized hardware instruction sets.

The ecs.u2i-c1m2.large instance is appropriate for low-traffic web serving, basic microservices, continuous integration build agents, containerized utility workers, and development or staging environments that operate within a 4.0 GB memory boundary.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2i-c1m2.large is a dedicated virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor, equipped with 2 dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon vCPUs operating at a 2.7 GHz clock speed and 4.0 GB of system memory. Providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this configuration provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, contains no bundled GPUs, and features no local instance storage, requiring remote block devices for persistent file operations. The dedicated vCPU model avoids CPU contention common in shared architectures, offering dependable computational cycles for standard computing tasks. Because of its 4.0 GB memory envelope and absence of local high-speed storage, the instance is best matched with lightweight backend services, basic web server hosting, small reverse proxies, build validation routines, and non-memory-intensive batch jobs that require stable compute resources.
